canonical_policy.name: Production containers use an appropriate runtime image
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: For production containers, use an appropriate runtime image rather than the SDK image solely for convenience, and avoid switching to root merely to bypass filesystem problems.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Runtime/nonroot/ownership duties covered; EXTRA0106/0109/0114 and BF0066..0068 cover multistage, probe executable, dockerignore and specialized-image verification.

context_quotes:
By default, production containers use an appropriate runtime image (the ASP.NET
runtime image for ASP.NET Core) rather than the SDK image for convenience, and do
not switch to root merely to bypass filesystem permission problems.

Keep build tooling out of production runtime images, keep images reproducible
and configuration external, keep Docker concerns separate from application
architecture, and use the deployment platform's health-probe capabilities when
practical.

Use a multi-stage build:

Copy only repository-level build files that exist and are required by restore.
Copy project files required for restore explicitly; avoid fragile wildcard
tricks that flatten or rearrange a multi-project structure.

## Restore Caching

Copy project and build dependency files before the full source tree so source
changes do not invalidate NuGet restore layers. Update the project-copy section
when the solution structure changes; do not optimize caching at the cost of a
Dockerfile that no longer restores the actual project graph.

Use the ASP.NET runtime image for ASP.NET Core applications and an appropriate
.NET runtime image for workers that do not need ASP.NET Core.

Use the built-in non-root user of modern .NET images when it fits:

Ensure directories the application writes to have the right ownership and
permissions, and find out why permissions are wrong instead of switching users.

Expose liveness/readiness endpoints through ASP.NET Core health checks
(`health-check` skill) and prefer native HTTP probes supplied by the
orchestrator. Do not assume the runtime image contains `curl`, `wget`, or shell
utilities; if Compose must run an in-container health command, verify the
executable exists or add an appropriate probe mechanism, weighing the cost of
installing debugging packages into a production image.

## Angular Container

When the Angular frontend is deployed as a static application, build it in a Node
build stage and serve the generated assets with the selected hosting strategy.
Nginx is not mandatory; the platform may provide static hosting directly. Keep
API base URLs and environment configuration compatible with the deployment
strategy.

## `.dockerignore`

Exclude files that do not belong in the build context:

```text
.git
.vs
**/bin
**/obj
**/node_modules
TestResults
coverage
```

Do not exclude tests when the image build intentionally runs them, and never
exclude files required by restore/build.

## Image Optimization

Start with standard supported .NET runtime images. Consider Alpine, chiseled
images, trimming, Native AOT, or other size optimizations only when
compatibility and deployment requirements justify them, and verify
globalization, native dependencies, reflection, diagnostics, and other runtime
behavior when using specialized images.

Avoid arbitrary infrastructure services in Compose, assuming curl/wget in
runtime images, specialized image variants without compatibility verification,
and Docker-specific changes leaking into Domain or Application code.

- When Serilog is configured, use by default the modern DI-integrated
  `builder.Services.AddSerilog(...)` approach rather than `UseSerilog`, keep

Avoid putting provider-specific APIs throughout Application code, dumping full
objects without review, and using logs as an audit database unless a dedicated
audit design has been adopted.

1. Use two-stage initialization when startup logging matters: a bootstrap
   logger captures failures before the full DI/configuration pipeline exists.
   Simpler applications may use normal host-managed Serilog setup without
   bootstrap logging.
2. `builder.Services.AddSerilog()` integrates with DI services through
   `ReadFrom.Services(services)`.
3. Message templates (`{PropertyName}`) create queryable structured data; string
   disabled.
4. Keep log levels, sinks, and overrides in configuration so they can change per
   environment without redeployment.
5. Keep direct Serilog APIs such as `Log.Logger` and `LogContext` at composition
   or provider-specific boundaries.

When the application uses Serilog's static/bootstrap `Log.Logger`, flush it on
shutdown so buffered events (Seq, OTLP, Elasticsearch sinks) are written:

```csharp
try { app.Run(); }
catch (Exception ex) { Log.Fatal(ex, "Unhandled exception"); }
finally { await Log.CloseAndFlushAsync(); }
```

For purely host-managed logging, follow the configured provider's lifetime
behavior instead of adding static Serilog lifecycle code.

The `Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch` package is deprecated. Use the official
`Elastic.Serilog.Sinks` package, which writes ECS-formatted documents to data
streams:

| Scenario | Recommendation |
|----------|---------------|
| Project uses Serilog as provider | `AddSerilog()` + configuration |
| Log storage (development) | Seq (free single-user) or Aspire Dashboard |
| Log storage (production) | Seq, Elasticsearch (Elastic sink), or an OTLP backend |
| Request logging | `UseSerilogRequestLogging()` |
| Scoped properties | `LogContext.PushProperty()` in middleware |
| Log filtering | `Serilog.Expressions` |
| High-performance paths | `[LoggerMessage]` source generator |
| Audit trails | `AuditTo` (synchronous, exceptions propagate) |
| Log levels by environment | `MinimumLevel.Override` per namespace in appsettings |
| OpenTelemetry integration | `Serilog.Sinks.OpenTelemetry` (no SDK dependency) |
